title: Bellman-Ford & negative cycles
overview: Bellman-Ford finds single-source shortest paths even with negative edge weights. It simply relaxes every edge n−1 times. One more round that still improves a distance proves a negative cycle, where no shortest path exists.

concepts.explain: Bellman-Ford loops over all edges, so an edge list (`a`, `b`, `c`) is the natural storage; here each edge is an `Edge` object.
A shortest path uses at most n−1 edges, so n−1 full rounds are enough to settle every distance.
Skip edges whose start is still infinite; otherwise `INT_MAX + c` overflows.
Run one extra round. If any edge still relaxes, a cycle with negative total weight is reachable.
O(V·E): slower than Dijkstra, but it handles negative edges.

files.title: Bellman-Ford
files.what: Stores directed weighted edges and relaxes all of them n−1 times from source 0, then prints the distances.
steps: Read edges into `edge_list` as `Edge(a, b, c)`.
Repeat n−1 times: for every edge, if `dis[a]` is known and `dis[a] + c < dis[b]`, update `dis[b]`.
files.input_note: `n e`, then e lines `a b c` (directed). Edge 2→1 has weight -3.
files.output_note: The real output is a compile error. With the fix it prints `1->2` (0→2→1 = 5 − 3, cheaper than the direct 4) and `3->4`.
files.watch_out: The file does **not compile**: `vector<Edge> edge_list;` appears before `class Edge` is declared, so the compiler does not know `Edge` yet. Fix: move the `class Edge { ... };` block above the `edge_list` line.

check.a: A shortest path without cycles has at most n−1 edges, and each round fixes at least one more edge of it.

files.title: Bellman-Ford with negative cycle check
files.what: After the n−1 rounds it does one more pass; any improvement means a negative cycle, otherwise it prints the distances.
steps: Extra pass: if any edge can still relax, set `cycle = true` and stop.
Print the cycle message, or the distances when there is none.
files.input_note: 3 nodes; edges 1→2 (−4) and 2→1 (+1) form a cycle of total −3.
files.output_note: The real output is a compile error. With the fix it prints `Negative weighted cycle detected`.
files.watch_out: The file does **not compile**: `vector<Edge> edge_list;` appears before `class Edge` is declared, so the compiler does not know `Edge` yet. Fix: move the `class Edge { ... };` block above the `edge_list` line.

check.q: Why is there no shortest path when a negative cycle is reachable?
check.a: Going around the cycle again always lowers the cost, forever.

files.watch_out: The copied driver declares `int t;` and then calls `cin.ignore()` instead of `cin >> t;`, so `t` holds garbage (on this run the loop did not run at all). Fix: `cin >> t;`. The solution class itself is fine.

check.q: Why does GFG use 10^8 as infinity instead of `INT_MAX`?
check.a: Adding a weight to 10^8 cannot overflow an `int`, and it is the value the judge expects for unreachable nodes.

recap: One extra round that still relaxes = negative cycle.

check_yourself.q: Bellman-Ford vs Dijkstra: which is faster, and which handles negative weights?
check_yourself.a: Dijkstra is faster (O((V+E) log V)); Bellman-Ford handles negative weights (O(V·E)).

check_yourself.q: For an undirected graph with a negative edge, what does Bellman-Ford report?
check_yourself.a: A negative cycle, because the edge can be walked back and forth.
Yes: if a full round changes nothing, all distances are final.
